key_insight: Spin-qubit quantum computers could become energy-competitive with classical computing before achieving an execution-time advantage.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing control-signal demultiplexing could reduce fault-tolerant system energy costs by approximately 100×, making control architecture a critical design choice.
method: Model the energy budget of a Loss–DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer.
Compare quantum Fourier transform energy and runtime against classical FFT under polynomially bounded sampling.
Include surface-code error correction, gate synthesis, and decoding costs.
evidence_signal: The model estimates approximately 100 kW for one million physical qubits, at least 10× below today's highest-performance classical computing systems.
watch_item: These are model-based estimates; instrumentation and decoding dominate at scale, while cryogenic cooling constrains scalability.
paper_title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
